I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is still the cropping pattern I trust most for steady grain output, easier sales, and work that I know how to manage well at my age. I would not spread myself into too many crops. With a middle-school education and practical experience, I would rather do two familiar grain crops properly than chase something more complicated and take market or management risk.

So for this year, I will carry the winter wheat through to harvest, then I will follow immediately with summer maize on the same land. I will use improved wheat seed because it is stable and easier to manage, and hybrid maize because the yield is worth it here. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer plus a topdressing at jointing, irrigate at the key water periods, and keep disease and aphid control to a small number of timely sprays. After wheat harvest, I will direct-seed maize quickly, keep the field clean, feed it mainly with nitrogen plus some phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate when the summer rain is not enough. I will keep tillage simple: rotary tillage for wheat preparation, then no-tillage for summer maize after wheat so I save time and moisture.
